validation.semantics: hold.chief_of_staff says « Envoyez un message dans sa conversation pour le recevoir / les recevoir », and _unlinked says « Retrouvez sa conversation dans la barre latérale et envoyez-y un message … ». Both name sending as the release action, and neither implies that opening is enough or that the messages were refused, failed, read or lost (« attend/attendent »). « cheffe de cabinet » matches ui.onboarding greeting_done/greeting_owed (8 occurrences in fr, no « chef de cabinet » drift). The feminine form follows the English she/her persona in onboarding and is correct. « barre latérale » is the existing fr term for sidebar, « sa conversation » echoes onboarding, and « Écrire à » matches the repo precedent ui.projects.project_links.message_title « Écrire à {title} » for « Message {title} ». It renders 'Message' as a verb and implies navigation rather than sending. The notices say « votre cheffe de cabinet » and the button says « la cheffe de cabinet », which is natural and consistent. Register is vous, imperative and sentence case, per the style guide. « pour le recevoir » keeps the English's own implicit-subject construction, so it is not a defect.
validation.icu: Parsed en and fr with @formatjs/icu-messageformat-parser (worktree node_modules, run from the scratchpad). For both plural keys the only argument is `count`, the plural selector is `count`, and {count} appears as an argument in every arm (fr one/many/other, en one/other). hold.open has no arguments in either locale. Key set and order equal the English (87 keys); the 84 base keys are value-identical to HEAD, and the diff only appends the three hold keys.
validation.plurals: Intl.PluralRules('fr') gives one/many/other, which matches the arms and the guide; there is no `few`. Formatted with intl-messageformat (fr) for 0, 1, 2, 5, 21, 1000000, 1500000 and 2000000: 0 and 1 give « message attend … le recevoir »; 2, 5, 21 and 1500000 give « messages attendent … les recevoir »; 1000000 and 2000000 give « de messages attendent … les recevoir ». Verb and pronoun agree in every arm. As in the English source, {count} is a simple argument and renders without grouping (e.g. 1000000); this is source-driven and does not matter at realistic counts.
